title: Operations Control Standards: Schedule-Change and Partner Rebooking Thresholds
content:
**Operations Control standards table — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** Two thresholds govern rebooking after an irregular operation: the size of a schedule shift that makes a schedule change significant, and how late the earliest Crestline alternative must arrive before rebooking on a partner carrier is offered.

| Fare brand | Significant schedule change, domestic itinerary (hours) | Significant schedule change, international itinerary (hours) | Partner rebooking offered when the earliest Crestline alternative arrives at least (hours after the original scheduled arrival) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Crestline Basic Economy | 3 | 6 | 6 |
| Crestline Main Cabin | 3 | 6 | 4 |
| Crestline Main Plus | 3 | 6 | 4 |
| Crestline Main Flexible | 3 | 6 | 3 |
| Crestline Premium Economy | 3 | 6 | 2 |
| Crestline First | 3 | 6 | 2 |

## Reading the thresholds

- A departure or arrival shift of at least 3 hours on a domestic itinerary, or at least 6 hours on an international itinerary, is significant; the threshold itself counts as significant. The shift is measured by the arrival lateness recorded on the disruption record.
- Partner rebooking is offered only when the earliest Crestline alternative arrives at least the stated number of hours after the original scheduled arrival.

**Boundary cases (hypothetical).** A domestic shift of exactly 3 hours is significant; a shift of 2 hours 59 minutes is not. On a Crestline Main Cabin ticket, a Crestline alternative arriving 4 hours late meets the partner threshold and one arriving 3 hours 30 minutes late does not; on Crestline Premium Economy the 3 hour 30 minute case meets it.
